newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1996 inflation forecast lowered - Reuter poll.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1996 inflation forecast lowered - Reuter poll.

text.p: Inflation expectations among Polish banks fell in September for the third month in a row, a monthly Reuter poll of the country's 24 biggest banks showed on Tuesday.
Banks predicted year-on-year inflation at the end of this year at 18.6 percent on average, against 18.7 last month, and the government's inflation target of 17 percent.
Banks expected the average yield of the benchmark 52-week T-bill at the end of the year to stay just above the 18.6 percent inflation rate, some 0.2 point lower than predicted last month.
At the last primary auction the average yield of the benchmark 52-week bills was 19.42 percent.

The 13-week T-bill yield and the three-month interbank deposit offered rate, used in T-bond coupons and credit interest calculations, were seen easing by December to 18.2 percent and 18.6 percent respectively from the current 18.6 percent and 19.4 percent.

Banks kept their dollar/zloty exchange rate expectations, virtually flat from last month predicting the zloty would trade at 2.8527 to the dollar at the end of 1996, against August's 2.8525 per dollar average.
The central bank fixed the zloty at 2.7760 per dollar on Tuesday.
